st: Mix half of the sliced red onion with the lime juice, half of the tomato, a handful of cilantro, and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Set aside to pickle while you make the soup.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the remaining onion, the bell pepper, and garlic for 5 minutes.
Stir in the remaining tomato and the cumin and cook 3 minutes.
Add [[8 cups]] water, [[1.5 tsp]] salt, the pepper, and the cassava. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 25 minutes until the cassava is tender.
Add the tuna chunks to the pot and simmer gently for 8 to 10 minutes, until the fish is opaque and cooked through (145°F / 63°C).
Lift out the tuna, flake it into large pieces, and return it to the pot.
Taste the broth and add a little salt if needed. Stir in half of the remaining cilantro.
Ladle into bowls and top with the pickled onion mixture and remaining cilantro. Serve with lime and crunchy plantain chips.
Soak the sliced red onion in cold water for 10 minutes, then drain. This softens its bite.
Bring [[6 cups]] water and a big pinch of salt to a boil in a pot.
Add the shrimp and cook for 2 minutes just until pink and curled. Drain and cool in a bowl of ice water for 3 minutes.
Drain the shrimp well and cut each into 2 or 3 pieces if large.
In a large bowl mix the lime juice, orange juice, [[2 tbsp]] ketchup, [[2 tbsp]] oil, [[1 tsp]] salt, and hot sauce to taste.
Add the shrimp, tomatoes, onion, and cilantro and stir well.
Chill for at least 30 minutes so the flavors blend. Keep it cold until serving.
Taste and adjust the salt and lime. Serve in bowls with popcorn, plantain chips, or rice.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 to 25 minutes until very tender. Drain well and let the steam rise off for 5 minutes.
Cook the onion in [[2 tbsp]] butter for 4 minutes until soft.
Mash the potatoes until smooth and mix in the cooked onion and [[1 tsp]] salt. Cool until you can handle it.
Divide into 12 balls. Press a hole in each, add a spoonful of cheese, and close the potato around it.
Flatten each ball into a patty about 1/2 inch thick.
For the sauce, blend the peanuts, milk, [[1 tbsp]] butter, [[0.5 tsp]] salt, and pepper until smooth, then warm in a pan over low heat for 5 minutes.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil and [[2 tbsp]] butter in a skillet and cook the patties 4 to 5 minutes per side until golden and crisp, in batches.
Fry the eggs in the same pan with the last [[1 tbsp]] oil until the whites are set.
Serve the patties with the eggs, avocado slices, and warm peanut sauce.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and cumin and stir for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes and [[4 cups]] water with [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer covered for 20 minutes until very tender.
Mash some of the potatoes against the side of the pot with a spoon, leaving some chunks.
Pour in the [[2 cups]] milk and half of the cheese. Simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Season with the remaining salt and the pepper. Do not boil hard, or the milk may curdle.
Ladle into bowls and top with the remaining cheese, avocado slices, and cilantro.
Put the salt cod in a pot with water to cover, simmer 10 minutes, drain, and repeat once to remove the salt. Flake the fish and remove any bones.
Simmer the pumpkin in [[3 cups]] of the water for 15 minutes until soft. Mash it in its cooking water into a coarse puree.
Melt [[3 tbsp]] butter in a large pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, rice, and the remaining [[3 cups]] water. Simmer 20 minutes.
Add the lima beans, white beans, corn, and peas and simmer 15 minutes more.
Stir in the pumpkin puree, then the ground peanuts and [[3 cups]] milk.
Add the flaked cod and [[1.5 tsp]] salt, if needed. Simmer gently for 20 minutes, stirring often so it does not scorch.
Stir in the cheese until melted. The soup should be thick but pourable. Add hot water if too thick.
Ladle into bowls and top with sliced hard-boiled egg.
Blend the garlic, cumin, onion, orange juice, beer, [[1 tbsp]] salt, pepper, and [[3 tbsp]] oil into a smooth marinade.
Poke the pork all over with a knife tip. Rub the marinade into the meat and into the cuts.
Marinate in the fridge for at least 4 hours, or overnight, turning once.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Put the pork in a roasting pan with [[1 cup]] water and cover tightly with foil.
Roast for 3 hours, basting with the pan juices every hour.
Add the potatoes to the pan, uncover, raise the oven to 400°F (200°C), and roast 35 to 40 minutes until the skin is crisp and the pork reaches at least 195°F (90°C).
Rest the pork for 15 minutes.
Slice or shred the pork and serve with the roasted potatoes and pan juices, plus pickled onion or hominy.
Peel the plantains with a knife and cut into thick chunks.
Boil in water with [[1 tsp]] salt for 20 minutes until fork-tender. Drain well.
Mash the hot plantains with [[2 tbsp]] butter and [[0.5 tsp]] salt until smooth with a few lumps.
Cool for 5 minutes until you can handle the mash. Divide into 8 balls.
Press a hole in half of the balls and fill with cheese, and the rest with the crumbled pork. Close and reshape into smooth balls.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Fry the bolones for 4 to 5 minutes per side until golden brown and crisp.
Fry the eggs in the same pan until the whites are set and serve the bolones with the eggs and coffee.
Blend the tomatoes, onion, bell pepper, cilantro, garlic, cumin, oregano, and [[1.5 tsp]] salt until smooth.
Rub the chicken with half of the blended sauce and the pepper. Marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a wide pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken for 4 minutes per side. Remove to a plate.
Pour the remaining sauce and the beer into the pot, scrape the bottom, and bring to a simmer.
Return the chicken. Cover and cook on low for 35 to 40 minutes, turning once, until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Meanwhile, heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a pot, stir in the rice for 1 minute, then add [[3 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Boil until the water reaches the rice, cover, and cook on the lowest heat for 18 minutes. Rest 5 minutes and fluff.
Serve the chicken and sauce over the rice with a side of avocado or salad.

ing: such as snapper, sea bass or cod, cut in large pieces
st: Season the fish with the lime juice, [[0.5 tsp]] salt, and half of the pepper. Let it sit 10 minutes.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, cumin, and paprika and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until they break down.
Pour in the coconut milk, [[1 tsp]] salt, and the remaining pepper. Simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Lay the fish in the sauce, spoon sauce over the top, cover, and cook for 8 to 10 minutes until opaque and flaking, 145°F (63°C).
Scatter the cilantro over the top, taste the sauce, and serve with white rice and fried plantains.
Soak the corn husks in hot water for 20 minutes until pliable, then drain.
Cook the onion in [[1 tbsp]] of the butter for 4 minutes until soft.
Blend the corn kernels in a food processor into a thick, slightly coarse puree.
Mix in the onion, eggs, remaining [[3 tbsp]] melted butter, cornmeal, [[1 tbsp]] sugar, baking powder, and [[1 tsp]] salt. Fold in the cheese.
Lay a husk flat with the pointed end facing you and spoon about [[0.33 cup]] of the mixture in the center.
Fold the sides over the filling, then fold up the bottom. Tie with a strip of husk if you like.
Set a steamer basket over simmering water and stack the humitas inside, folded sides down.
Cover and steam for 45 minutes, adding hot water if the pot runs low, until firm.
Let the humitas rest for 10 minutes, then unwrap and eat warm with coffee.
Mix the flour, baking powder, and [[1 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Beat the egg with [[4 tbsp]] melted butter and [[0.5 cup]] warm water, pour into the flour, and knead for 5 minutes to a smooth, soft dough.
Cover the dough and rest it for 20 minutes.
Toss the cheese with the scallions in a bowl.
Roll the dough about 1/8 inch thick and cut out 4-inch circles. Re-roll scraps.
Put a heaping spoonful of cheese in the middle of each circle, fold in half, and press the edges with a fork to seal tightly.
Heat [[4 cups]] oil in a deep pot to 365°F (185°C).
Fry 3 or 4 at a time for 2 to 3 minutes per side until puffed and golden.
Drain on paper towels and dust with the [[3 tbsp]] sugar while hot. Serve warm.
Put [[1 cup]] of the pineapple, the cinnamon, cloves, allspice, orange peel, and [[8 cups]] water into a pot. Boil, then simmer for 20 minutes.
Strain the spiced liquid into a clean pot and discard the solids.
Blend the blackberries with [[1 cup]] water, then press through a strainer into the pot to remove the seeds.
Whisk the purple corn flour into [[0.5 cup]] cold water until smooth.
Pour the corn mixture into the pot while whisking, bring to a simmer, and cook for 15 minutes, stirring often, until thickened.
Add [[0.75 cup]] sugar and stir until dissolved, then taste and adjust.
Add the remaining diced pineapple and the strawberries and simmer 5 minutes.
Serve warm in mugs with a few fruit pieces in each, traditionally with sweet bread.
